text:
Vancouver arrives in Sunrise with the weaker underlying numbers on both ends. The Canucks have generated 2.53 expected goals per 60 and allowed 3.64, and they hold just 42 percent of the quality chances at 5-on-5, which fits a team that has allowed 4.75 goals a game over eight games. Florida sits at 3.23 for and 3.11 against, a 52 percent share, so the Panthers have been the better side by chance quality even with only 2.71 goals a game to show for it. The model projects 4.08 expected goals for Florida tonight against 2.87 for Vancouver.

Special teams may tilt this further. Florida's power play is producing 1.42 expected goals per game and the Panthers draw 6.43 penalties a game, while Vancouver takes 4.0 a game and has a 1.03 expected goals against per game on the kill, identical to Florida's. In goal, projected starter Kevin Lankinen has stopped 78 percent of shots this season and sits at minus 11.11 goals saved above expected, after a minus 20.31 mark across 47 games last year. Projected Florida starter Jacob Markstrom is at plus 2.49 in five games, though he was minus 15.98 last season.

On form, Vancouver has dropped five straight, allowing 6 to the Rangers and 7 to Carolina, and plays on one day of rest. Florida beat Columbus 7-3 in its last outing after a 5-3 loss at Buffalo. The model likes Sam Reinhart to score at 46 percent, with Matthew Tkachuk (37 percent) and Brady Tkachuk (36 percent) behind him. Matthew Tkachuk is also given a 46 percent chance at two or more points. For Vancouver, Jake DeBrusk leads at 28 percent to score, with Elias Pettersson at 21 percent for a multi-point night.
